# You should be able to take out your money. Right now, you can’t.

*By Inês, Product Designer at Pinha*  
*Tuesday, 10 November 2026*

Since Friday morning, you have not been able to withdraw your money from Pinha. Our payments partner, Northvale Payments, blocked all outgoing transfers. Deposits and round-ups have stopped too.

Your money is not lost. It remains in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money, and Northvale cannot use it for its own purposes. But we cannot move it until Northvale releases it.

That distinction matters. It also does nothing to pay your rent today.

I’m Inês. I’m a product designer at Pinha, and I write most of the words you see in the app. I designed the screen that says, “Your money is always yours, take it out anytime.”

I look at that screen now and feel sick. It is a promise you relied on, and right now we are not delivering on it.

You deserve a clear explanation of what happened, what we are doing and what you can do today. You also deserve an apology. I’m sorry you have been left without access to your own money.

## If you need your money urgently

**If the freeze is affecting rent, medical needs or your ability to manage after losing your job, email urgent@pinha.example with the subject line URGENTE.**

We are trying to obtain individual releases from Northvale for urgent cases. **We cannot guarantee a release or tell you when one will happen.** But we want these cases identified so we can push for them individually.

Our support team has received around 1,900 emails since Friday, 6 November. There are three people answering them, and the current reply time is approximately two days. If you are waiting for an answer, that is why. It does not mean your message is unimportant.

**We have cancelled the monthly fee for November and December for everyone.** That will not make up for being unable to access your savings. We should not be charging you while this is happening.

## What happened

Northvale Payments is an e-money institution based in Vilnius. It is the partner that holds Pinha customers’ money.

On **Wednesday, 4 November**, Northvale emailed us a notice of “commercial termination,” giving us 30 days’ notice. The explanation it gave was a “risk appetite review.” We have not received a substantive explanation beyond that.

Then, at **09:00 on Friday, 6 November**, Northvale blocked all outgoing transfers without warning. That was not what its notice said would happen. Deposits and round-ups stopped as well.

A notice period should give us time to arrange a transition. Instead, two days after receiving that notice, we had users unable to withdraw their money.

We are angry about that. There is a real difference between ending a commercial relationship and abruptly cutting people off from their savings. You are the ones living with the consequences of Northvale’s decision.

On **Saturday, 7 November**, we filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and the Lithuanian central bank.

Rui, our CEO, is working with lawyers and is in discussions with Banco de Portugal. We have also signed a new payments partner, Ostra Bank, based in Lisbon.

That is where things stand today. The new partner is signed. The transfer of your balances has not happened yet.

## Where your money is

Your money is held in a safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own funds. Northvale cannot use it as its own money.

**The money is not lost. The problem is access: Northvale has blocked outgoing transfers, and we cannot move the funds until it releases them.**

I want to be precise here because saying “your money is safe” without explaining the rest would leave out the thing that matters most to you today. Safeguarding does not mean you can currently make a withdrawal. It does not give us a way around the block.

You should not have to learn how a payments partnership works to understand why you cannot get to your savings. But you deserve to know both where the money is and what is preventing it from reaching you.

## How we plan to restore access

We have signed with **Ostra Bank in Lisbon** to move Pinha to a new payments partner.

For that migration to proceed, we need Northvale to provide the balances file, and we need approval from Banco de Portugal. Signing a replacement partner is an important step, but it does not remove those dependencies.

**Our current estimate for the migration is 10 to 15 working days. This is an estimate, not a confirmed completion window or a promised withdrawal date.** It depends on steps we do not control, and it may change.

We cannot honestly give you a day when everyone will have access again. I know that is a deeply frustrating answer when you need to make plans. Giving you a date we cannot stand behind would make those plans even harder.

We will tell you when the remaining steps are completed, and we will tell you if the estimate changes.

## Our part in this

Northvale made the decision to block transfers. We made the decision to rely on one payments partner without a backup.

That was our mistake.

We were naive about what relying on a single partner could mean for you. We cannot put all the responsibility elsewhere simply because we did not press the button that stopped withdrawals. We built a savings app around the expectation that you could take your money out when you needed it. Our setup has failed to keep that expectation.

Pinha has around 14,200 active users, mostly in Portugal and some in Spain. Each balance belongs to someone with their own plans and pressures. Having thousands of people affected does not make any one person’s situation smaller.

You are entitled to be angry with Northvale. You are entitled to be angry with us too. I’m not going to ask you to calm down or be patient as though patience pays a bill.

## We are reading what you send us

One person in Porto wrote to us in capital letters. She had saved for three years for a car deposit. The dealership has given her until **Friday, 13 November**.

I read her email on the metro and nearly cried.

I am sharing that without identifying her because it makes the stakes clear. These are savings people have worked for, sometimes for years. A delay can mean losing something they have been working towards, not simply waiting a little longer.

And I cannot tell her, or anyone else facing a deadline this week, that we will have this resolved by Friday. We do not know that.

What we can do is keep pursuing individual releases for urgent cases, work through the migration requirements and answer as clearly as we can. Our feelings about this are not a substitute for getting your money moving again.

## What happens next

Here is what you can expect from us:

- **Urgent cases:** email **urgent@pinha.example**, using **URGENTE** as the subject. We are seeking individual releases, but cannot guarantee them.
- **Support replies:** our current reply time is approximately **two days**, with three people handling around 1,900 emails received since Friday.
- **Fees:** the monthly fee is cancelled for **November and December**, for everyone.
- **Public updates:** we will publish an update on this blog **every Monday and Thursday until this is resolved**, including when there is no confirmed progress to report.

The next scheduled update is **Thursday, 12 November**.

We will keep separating what has happened from what we hope will happen. A request is not an approval. An estimate is not a deadline. A signed partner is not a completed migration.

You trusted Pinha with money you put aside. Right now, you cannot access it, and we owe you more than reassuring words. We owe you honest information and the work needed to restore that access.

— Inês
